title: Zero-Gap GPU Execution: Building Secure, Pre-Warmed Pod Runtimes for High-Velocity AI Agents
tldr: LinkedIn built Firepool, a broker that keeps warm GPU pods ready so agents and RL loops running on CPU nodes can launch GPU jobs without Kubernetes pod startup in the critical path. Its zero-gap mode uses HAMi and Volcano to park standby pods on a busy GPU so the next job takes over the card the moment the current one ends.

key_points.text: Motivating workloads: Autopilot (an agent migrating TensorFlow models to PyTorch for tens of hours), an auto-research agent running experiments for days, and agentic RL rollouts. All need GPUs repeatedly but not continuously.
Running agents on GPU nodes wastes GPUs while they think; running them on CPU nodes and launching a GPU pod per step pays a cold start every iteration.

The Firepool broker has a REST API, job store and pool controller for capacity, plus a dispatcher, in-memory pod tracker and executors; each pod runs a lightweight Firepool agent that fetches and runs the job code.

The API is built for agents: submit returns a job ID immediately, unknown fields are rejected to block hallucinated input, retries stay under one job ID, and failures return a specific error class and exit code.

Pod selection order: the caller's own idle pod, then a never-used idle pod, then a standby on a busy GPU, and only last a new pod. Claiming happens in one step under one lock; multi-pod jobs claim all pods at once, gang-style.
Pods start with a shared base image (CUDA, framework); user code, extra Python packages and distributed rank/addresses arrive with the job, so one pool serves many environments.
Safe reuse rules: verified reset of the process tree, code and shared memory (else delete the pod), owner-only reuse, and a reuse tag that marks a pod for retirement when a different tag lands on it.

Pools are sized from the job queue, not GPU utilization, with four knobs: floor, ceiling, idle wait time, and idle pods kept after that. Firepool can borrow idle GPUs from other teams and return them on demand.
Zero gap uses HAMi only for scheduling multiple pods per GPU (no partitioning or time sharing); one pod runs a job with the full card while standby pods wait to be promoted.

Sandboxing: pods have no egress by default; all outbound traffic goes through a sidecar proxy that holds the credentials, injects them and checks policy. A checkpoint daemon persists agent state, and shared memory lets agent instances share learnings.
Q&A: Firepool only uses spare capacity and does not run production training; fragmentation is handled with fixed GPU SKU types and custom Volcano bin-packing plugins.

numbers.text: New GPU pod cold start with cached image: 20-30 seconds; uncached image: 2-10 minutes.
Binding a job to a warm pod takes under half a second.
Median handover time with a different reuse tag per job dropped from 51 seconds to under a second.
A new GPU pod takes about 22 seconds to run its first instruction; on a warm pod job code starts in about a second.
In an H200 benchmark, an agent loop went from 26 minutes to 2.
19 of 20 pod requests in production are served from warm pods (standbys included).
Auto-research agent runs have lasted 7 days.
Autopilot cut TensorFlow-to-PyTorch migration time per model from months to about a week.

open_gaps.text: Standby pods with different container images on the same GPU are not supported yet; it is the next step, aimed at many RL environments on a small GPU budget.
When the cluster is full, plain warm pools cannot grow and jobs wait for capacity again; agents now mostly wait on quota rather than cold start.
Pod reuse is not a security boundary: state outside tracked writable paths is handled by read-only pods and opt-out, not full isolation.
Firepool is not open source yet; the team plans to release it.

opportunities.text: Add a warm-pod broker in front of GPU jobs for agent loops, sized from queue depth with floor and ceiling knobs.
Use HAMi scheduling slots with Volcano to park standby pods on busy GPUs and cut handover gaps between tenants.
Follow Firepool's planned open-source release and help with multi-image standby support.
Sidecar credential injection with no-egress pods as a pattern for running untrusted agent code.
